system_description.narrative_title: Israel-Gaza conflict internationalizes: diplomacy, security, and spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is the internationalization of the Israel–Gaza war and its political, diplomatic and security spillovers. Treated as an open system, the conflict links military operations, refugee/humanitarian flows, diplomatic actions (expulsions, UN dynamics), and transnational security incidents (suspected plots, arrests) through rapid information flows and feedback loops: strikes and political moves provoke diplomatic reactions and protests, which in turn shape allied responses and security postures across Europe and the Middle East. The system is sensitive to catalytic events (attacks, high-profile speeches, arrests) that quickly reconfigure alliances, legal measures, and domestic politics in multiple countries.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: Israel–Palestine military operations and political decisions, Israeli government actions (elections, diplomatic expulsions), UN and international diplomatic responses, Lebanese actor involvement (Hezbollah, displacement/housing projects), European security incidents linked to the conflict (e.g., RAF Fairford arrests), domestic protests and settler violence related to occupation and settlements.
system_description.super_system: Global security and diplomatic order (international relations, multilateral institutions, and transnational security frameworks)
adjacent_subsystems: European domestic security and counterterrorism (policing, arrests, investigations)
Multilateral institutions and international law (UN, sanctions, corporate listings)
Humanitarian and displacement systems in Lebanon and Gaza

variables.name: Armed conflict intensity
variables.description: The overall magnitude and tempo of kinetic military operations and violence within the conflict zone.

variables.name: Civilian displacement rate
variables.description: The rate at which civilians are forced to leave or are uprooted from their habitual residences within affected areas.

variables.name: Cross-border refugee flow
variables.description: The volume and velocity of people crossing international borders seeking refuge as a result of the conflict.

variables.name: Humanitarian aid delivery rate
variables.description: The frequency and quantity of delivered humanitarian assistance (food, shelter, medical supplies) into affected populations.

variables.name: Diplomatic tension level
variables.description: The prevailing intensity of bilateral and multilateral diplomatic friction, public rebukes, and formal complaints between external actors.

variables.name: Diplomatic sanctions and expulsions rate
variables.description: The frequency of formal diplomatic measures such as expulsions, sanctions, or suspension of relations enacted in response to the conflict.

variables.name: Multilateral engagement level
variables.description: The intensity of involvement and activity of multilateral processes and forums (deliberations, resolutions, investigations) addressing the crisis.

variables.name: Transnational security incident rate
variables.description: The rate at which suspected plots, attacks, arrests, and cross-border security incidents linked to the conflict occur outside the primary combat zone.

variables.name: Protest mobilization intensity
variables.description: The level and frequency of public demonstrations, counter-demonstrations, and street-level mobilization related to the conflict in multiple jurisdictions.

variables.name: Spillover violence rate
variables.description: The frequency and scale of localized violent incidents (including communal violence, reprisals, and settler-related attacks) in neighboring or connected areas.

variables.name: Allied security posture rigidity
variables.description: The degree to which allied and partner states harden military readiness, base security measures, and posture in response to the conflict.

variables.name: Information amplification velocity
variables.description: The speed and breadth at which conflict-related information, narratives, and imagery propagate across media and social networks.

variables.name: Foreign public polarization
variables.description: The degree of polarization and intensity of opinion among external publics regarding actors, actions, and policies tied to the conflict.

variables.name: Legal and accountability pressure intensity
variables.description: The strength and frequency of legal initiatives, investigations, company listings, and accountability mechanisms triggered by conflict-related actions.

variables.name: Border control stringency
variables.description: The strictness and enforcement intensity of cross-border controls, entry restrictions, and migration policies in response to security and refugee flows.

variables.name: Economic and energy market disruption level
variables.description: The magnitude of disruptions in trade, energy markets, critical supply chains, and economic activity attributable to the conflict and its spillovers.
